standard: Acceptable visible refinement at application scale; not a numerical quality rating or production release approval.

front.note: The softened seat and back and added metal supports improve construction, but the white seat welt visibly stops across the front and leaves loose-looking corner tails; changes required.

rear.note: Rear metal uprights now visibly connect the back cushion to the seat and legs. The rear-left seat welt also lifts locally above the cushion, so tailoring contact remains unresolved.

detail.note: Full-size detail confirms a broad missing front welt span and raised rear-left run. All 24 source sections need continuous seated contact rather than the current 16 transported sections.

underside.note: The black seat pan and four capped metal feet remain coherent from below; no new detached underside piece is visible. This acceptable structure does not resolve the upper-seat welt defect.

clay.note: The clay view shows a recognizable squared padded chair with softened corners and supported back. The overall silhouette is acceptable, but the material view exposes the broken piping clearly.

front.note: The staggered stack now has thin cover boards and recessed page blocks that read more clearly as books than the original rounded solid slabs; original book positions remain coherent.

rear.note: Rear cover lips and slim page edges form a continuous stack without visibly floating books. White upper bindings remain understated but the separate book layers are legible.

detail.note: Full-size detail shows fine paper-fiber texture, inset page edges, spine rules and small title panels. The inherited glossy blue binding and blank labels are acceptable at catalog scale.

underside.note: The green bottom cover and offset neighboring books form closed volumes from below; the exposed lips and pageblock boundaries remain connected rather than protruding as loose pieces.

clay.note: The clay view retains five individually readable books with sharper cover overhangs and layered thickness. Construction is visibly improved without changing the compact stack silhouette.

front.note: The charcoal base remains clean below the glass with restrained added casework detail. Fish, sand, stones and dense aquarium planting retain the accepted original arrangement; improvement is limited to exterior construction.

rear.note: The rear view retains the light bar, filter and layered plants inside aligned glass panels. No new casework obstructs the fish or intrudes into the visible aquascape.

detail.note: Full-size detail retains recognizable fish eyes, fins, bubbles, filter slots, stones and authored leaves. Their existing stylized appearance is preserved rather than claimed as a newly rebuilt interior.

underside.note: The underside is a continuous dark base plate with a coherent frame edge. The exterior additions remain visually contained below the glazing and do not create dangling hardware.

clay.note: The clay view preserves the rectangular tank, top frame and base silhouette without added bulk. This is acceptable as a conservative protected-model refinement, not a large fidelity upgrade.

front.note: Three aligned glazed leaves, slim white app-default frames and separate pull handles read immediately as the patio slider. The hardware surface refinement is modest; original construction remains recognizable.

rear.note: Rear rails, leaf spacing and frame thickness stay consistent across all three panels. No visibly detached handle or newly distorted sliding leaf appears in this static review.

detail.note: The full-size detail keeps the narrow metal handles distinct against even frosted glazing, with restrained surface response and no coarse normal-map bumps or damaged frame edges.

underside.note: The low view shows continuous perimeter and bottom track edges with all three panels seated together. Static renders do not establish sliding behavior, which remains a separate runtime check.

clay.note: The clay view retains clean repeated panel proportions and layered rails. The existing slim silhouette is acceptable; this is a material refinement rather than a major geometry redesign.

front.note: The left-chaise sectional keeps its accepted squared cushions, connected matte arms and small wood feet. Surface shading is restrained, without the strong pale sheen that obscured the selected upholstery tint.

rear.note: The rear panels and arm seams remain continuous and visually supported by the base. Existing cushion joints are orderly and no extra loose side cushion has been introduced.

detail.note: Full-size detail shows soft edge transitions and quiet upholstery grain around the chaise and seat joins. Tiny inherited gaps at back-cushion corners are acceptable at app scale; no coarse basket weave is visible.

underside.note: The two connected base sections and their wood feet remain coherent from below. The dark underside is closed and no new loose trim or floating fabric detail is apparent.

clay.note: The clay view retains the familiar left-chaise proportions and layered cushions. Geometry was already acceptable; the visible improvement is a calmer tinted material response rather than new construction.

front.note: The globe remains legible on its round pedestal with a restrained softened base edge and brass meridian ring. Geographic imagery is preserved; improvement is limited to base and hardware surfaces.

rear.note: The reverse geography, complete ring and tapered stand remain aligned. The pedestal edge and circular inlay read cleanly without a visible gap between support and globe assembly.

detail.note: Full-size detail retains coastlines, ring ticks and the polar mounting pin. Fine brass grain is noticeable close up but does not obscure the scale marks; inherited globe faceting remains acceptable at app scale.

underside.note: The low view shows a closed circular pedestal underside and a centered support. No new floating base detail or changed globe clearance is visible.

clay.note: The clay view keeps the sphere, meridian arch and pedestal silhouette distinct. Protected rotating geometry is visually unchanged; these static images do not by themselves prove motion behavior.
